title: The Colony of New Lagos
premise: Yara Iversen keeps the New Lagos beacon running because the backups in the hold — copies of colonists who never woke — hum to him like a second heartbeat. When the ship Meridian returns from dead space with its crew aged backward into children, Yara discovers his beacon has been answering something out there for years, and that he himself may be one of the backups who woke wrong. As the fleet's fragile truce over the Meridian's return collapses, Yara and Meridian's eldest-again captain, Sefu Okonkwo, race to a relay at the edge of dead space to broadcast the truth before the fleet fires on the colony. At the relay, Yara learns the signal was his own original self calling home; choosing love and belonging over duty, he lets the transmission merge with the beacon, ending the truce not with war but with every backup waking at once.
about_author: Gideon Crane is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent eleven years maintaining lighthouse beacons off the West African coast before turning to fiction. He writes science fiction about lonely signals, borrowed bodies, and the people who answer them.

chapters.title: The Hum Below Decks
chapters.summary: Yara Iversen's POV. On the colony world of New Lagos, Yara maintains an orbital beacon no record shows anyone commissioning, while the hold beneath the settlement holds hundreds of sleeping backups. He talks to them during night shifts. Emotional beat: tender loneliness, the sense of being caretaker to ghosts who might be family.

chapters.title: Meridian, Returning
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A long-lost deep-space ship, the Meridian, answers the beacon after thirty years — but everyone aboard has aged backward into children with adult eyes. The colony council seals the docking bay. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread as Yara recognizes a child officer who calls him by a name that isn't his.

chapters.title: The Truce Clock
chapters.summary: Sefu Okonkwo's POV. The fleet arrives to quarantine New Lagos, imposing a seventy-two-hour truce while it decides whether the Meridian's condition is contagion or weapon. Sefu, the fleet negotiator, meets Yara across a sealed airlock. Emotional beat: two dutiful strangers circling an attraction they refuse to name.

chapters.title: Children Who Remember
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Inside quarantine, the de-aged crew speaks in unison about 'the choir' they found in dead space, and one child tells Yara he was aboard once. Yara finds his own face in the Meridian's old crew manifest. Emotional beat: identity cracking open; the horror of possibly being a copy who replaced a man.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Answers
chapters.summary: Sefu's POV. Sefu decrypts fleet records showing the beacon predates the colony itself and has been transmitting toward dead space since before anyone arrived. The fleet hardliners move to seize the hold of backups as evidence. Emotional beat: Sefu choosing between career and conscience, drawn to Yara's quiet grief.

chapters.title: Seventy-Two Hours
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. With the truce half-expired, Yara and Sefu steal a courier skiff, taking a de-aged Meridian child as their guide to the relay at the edge of dead space. Behind them, the fleet moves on the colony. Emotional beat: fugitive intimacy — love admitted aloud somewhere past the last buoy.

chapters.title: Dead Space
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. In the silence beyond navigation charts, the child leads them through a reef of derelict ships, all decades old, all carrying backups. Yara's memories begin arriving that aren't his: launch day, a woman named Iversen, a promise to come back. Emotional beat: mourning a life he may have stolen or been stolen from.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: Sefu's POV. They reach the ancient relay and find it keyed to Yara's biometrics — built by his original self, who stayed behind in the choir to keep calling home. The fleet's ultimatum expires in hours; hardliner ships are already burning toward New Lagos. Emotional beat: terrible clarity — the truth can save the colony only if someone pays for it.

chapters.title: Signal and Sacrifice
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, climax. The relay demands a living navigator to carry the full broadcast — the choir's memory, the backups' names, proof the de-aging is transformation, not attack. Yara merges with the signal, letting his uncertain self dissolve into the beacon, while Sefu holds the channel open against jamming. Emotional beat: love against duty resolved by refusing the choice — giving both everything.

chapters.title: Everyone Waking at Once
chapters.summary: Sefu's POV, resolution. The broadcast reaches the fleet mid-assault; weapons stand down as the truth spreads, and across New Lagos the backups in the hold wake — including, impossibly, a version of Yara carrying every memory of the man who loved him. Sefu waits at the airlock. Emotional beat: belonging earned, identity chosen rather than assigned, dawn over a colony that finally knows why its beacon sings.
